The reducer needs NO code change: it already handles any state declared under recoverable_states generically (entry from any non-terminal state, resume only to the recorded state, never a genuine blocker because it is not `blocked`).

proposals.protected_class: V3 lifecycle contract + reducer (root of trust; owner-only)
proposals.purpose: ONE consolidated lifecycle change (21 §3 P3(a)(b)(c)(e)(g) + D3.5): (1) recoverable `technical_suspension` (P5 reasons + RECOVERY_EXHAUSTED, RESOURCE_WAIT_EXCEEDED); (2) re-verification back-edge publishing -> testing (reason APPROVALS_EXPIRED) that invalidates the approvals it replaces; (3) terminal, owner-only `cancelled` (never after merge); (4) waiting_external PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and waiting_subscription BILLING_REVERIFICATION_REQUIRED (never blockers); (5) the blocked-state escape fix: a STICKY owner hold set on entering blocked, kept across every recoverable hop (waiting, paused, recovery, suspension) and fencing/head events, cleared only by an owner action or an owner cancellation; (6) D3.5 independent-verification F2: a `dependency_rebuild` back-edge (testing | independent_review | security_review | publishing -> implementing, reason DEPENDENCY_CHANGED) that invalidates the approvals a task obtained on a dependency basis that later CHANGED — the task is rebuilt and re-verified, never re-attested. Without it the authoritative lifecycle fails closed.
proposals.verified: tests/d35-lifecycle-proposal.test.mjs applies P6 to a DISPOSABLE copy of the real reducer + contract and drives it: every direct/indirect/paused/recovery/suspension/fenced hop out of blocked is refused without an owner action; cancellation, re-verification and the new reasons; and the ENGINE end to end in a labelled proposal configuration (proposalReducer, temp ledgers only). The authoritative reducer is unchanged (a test proves the old loophole is still there and that the controller never uses it).
proposals.effects: changes the lifecycle contract digest the policy bootstrap pins AND the reducer code (authority-adjacent, pinned in the dh3 closure); after the owner applies it and re-pins, the D3.5 engine paths that are gated on the contract (technical_suspension state, reverification, explicit cancellation) activate with no further code change. Owner-action AUTHENTICITY is a separate gate (G-OWNER-ACTION-EVIDENCE): the reducer can only require that an owner_action_id is present.

Contract: safeguarded, requires_activation, NOT active actions open_draft_pull_request, update_pull_request_metadata, rerun_ci_jobs, dispatch_staging_candidate (identity trusted_publisher), each with the delivery_target check; the three EXISTING D3.2 actions (publish_candidate_branch, mark_pull_request_ready, verify_delivery_eligibility) are byte-for-byte UNCHANGED, so every D3.2 authority test keeps its meaning (their delivery-target binding and publish's independent-review requirement stay in the delivery layer until a follow-up changes them together with their tests, residual R-31); new single-use approval evidence ci_failure_diagnosis and staging_admission (issued by delivery_verifier, so no action approves itself) and owner_decision (task_ingress). Evidence: an optional signed `decision` {action, owner_action_id} for owner_decision (G-OWNER-ACTION-EVIDENCE).
